ai.literal: Brightness lost, that-became-dull eyes too; he went days having-touched, that-wore-away fingers.
ai.translation: My eyes have lost their brightness and grown dull, and my fingers are worn away from touching the marks to count the days since he left.
ai.modern: அவர் பிரிந்து சென்ற நாட்களைத் தொட்டு எண்ணி என் விரல்கள் தேய்ந்துவிட்டன; அவர் வரும் வழியைப் பார்த்து என் கண்களும் ஒளியிழந்து மங்கிவிட்டன.
ai.explanation: The speaker expresses the physical toll of her prolonged yearning for her lover's return. Her eyes have lost their natural luster from constantly watching the road for him. Meanwhile, her fingers have worn down from the daily habit of touching marks to count the days since his departure. The vivid imagery of dull eyes and worn fingers emphasizes the sheer length of the separation and the depth of her longing.

ai.literal: Shining O jeweled one! Today if I forget, my shoulder upon ornaments will slip off, beauty having left.
ai.translation: O friend with shining jewels! If I forget him today, my beauty will forsake me and the bangles will slip from my shoulders.
ai.modern: ஒளிரும் அணிகலன்களை அணிந்த தோழியே! இன்று நான் அவரை மறந்தால், என் அழகு என்னை விட்டு நீங்கும்; என் தோள்களில் உள்ள வளையல்களும் கழன்று விழும்.
ai.explanation: The heroine speaks to her friend, addressing her as one wearing shining jewels. She declares that she cannot forget her lover even for a moment. If she were to forget him today, she would instantly waste away in sorrow, causing her natural beauty to vanish and her bangles to slip from her thinning arms. The physical slipping of ornaments vividly illustrates the immediate physical toll of emotional separation.

ai.literal: Strength having desired, mind as companion, he who went; coming having desired, still I exist.
ai.translation: He departed, desiring success in his mission, with his own mind as his companion. I am still alive, desiring only his return.
ai.modern: வெற்றியை விரும்பித் தன் உள்ளத்தையே துணையாகக் கொண்டு சென்றவர், மீண்டும் திரும்பி வருவார் என்று விரும்பி நான் இன்னும் உயிரோடு இருக்கிறேன்.
ai.explanation: The heroine speaks of the contrasting desires that drive her and her lover. He left her because he desired 'uran' (strength of purpose or success in his mission), taking only his own determined mind as his companion. She, however, manages to stay alive only because she desires his 'varal' (return). The repeated word 'nacaii' (having desired) beautifully highlights how his desire for achievement separated them, while her desire for his return is the only thing keeping her alive.

ai.literal: Joined passion he-who-parted return thinking-of, branch taking climbs my heart.
ai.translation: Thinking of the return of my lover who parted after we enjoyed our passion, my heart climbs the highest branch.
ai.modern: நாம் கூடி மகிழ்ந்த காமத்தை நினைத்து, என்னைப் பிரிந்து சென்ற காதலர் திரும்பி வருவதை எண்ணி, என் நெஞ்சம் மரத்தின் உச்சிக்கொம்பில் ஏறிப் பார்க்கிறது.
ai.explanation: The speaker expresses her intense anticipation for her lover's return. She remembers the love they shared before he departed. Thinking of his imminent arrival, her heart is described as climbing the highest branch, a metaphor for looking out eagerly into the distance to catch the first glimpse of him. The word 'kōṭu' means a branch or peak, emphasizing the height of her eager expectation.

ai.literal: Let see indeed lover (acc.) eyes to be full; seen after, will leave my soft shoulders' pallor.
ai.translation: Let me just see my lover until my eyes are full. After I see him, the pallor on my soft shoulders will vanish.
ai.modern: என் கண்கள் குளிரும்படி என் காதலனை நான் காண்பேனாக. அவனைக் கண்ட பிறகு, என் மென்மையான தோள்களில் படர்ந்துள்ள பசலை நிறம் நீங்கிவிடும்.
ai.explanation: The speaker expresses a deep yearning to see her lover, wishing to feast her eyes upon him until they are completely satisfied. She is confident that the lovesick pallor ('pacappu') that has spread over her soft shoulders during his absence is only temporary. The phrase 'kaṇ āra' (eyes to be full) highlights the intensity of her longing, while the certainty that the pallor 'will leave' (nīṅkum) shows her belief in the healing power of his presence.

ai.literal: Let come indeed the lover one day; I will drink [him] for sorrowful pain all to perish.
ai.translation: If only my lover would return for just one day! I will drink him in, so that all my sorrowful pain perishes.
ai.modern: என் காதலர் ஒருநாள் வருவாராக! என்னுடைய துன்ப நோய் எல்லாம் அழியும்படி நான் அவரைப் பருகுவேன்.
ai.explanation: The speaker expresses a deep, consuming longing for her absent lover's return. She wishes for him to come back for just one day. To cure her lovesickness, she uses the striking metaphor of drinking him in ('பருகுவன்'), as if his presence is a healing draught. This intense visual and physical consumption is meant to completely destroy ('கெட') all her sorrow and pain ('பைதல் நோய்'). The word 'மன்' acts as a particle of intense wishing, emphasizing her desperate yearning.

ai.literal: Shall I sulk? Shall I embrace? Or shall I unite? Eye-like lover if comes.
ai.translation: When my lover, who is as precious as my own eyes, returns, shall I sulk? Shall I embrace him? Or shall I do both and unite with him?
ai.modern: என் கண்களைப் போன்ற காதலர் திரும்பி வந்தால், நான் அவரிடம் ஊடல் கொள்வேனா? அல்லது அவரைத் தழுவுவேனா? அல்லது ஊடலும் தழுவலும் கலந்து அவரோடு இணைவேனா?
ai.explanation: The speaker eagerly anticipates the return of her lover, who is as essential and dear to her as her own eyes. She playfully debates with herself about how she will react when he finally arrives. She wonders whether she should feign anger for his long absence, simply embrace him out of joy, or mingle both reactions together. This internal debate highlights her overwhelming love and the restless excitement of her waiting.

ai.literal: Battle having joined, having won, let grant king; home having joined, evening let us perform feast.
ai.translation: Let the king engage in battle, win, and grant me leave. Then I shall return home and celebrate a feast this evening.
ai.modern: அரசன் போரில் கலந்து கொண்டு வென்று எனக்கு விடை தரட்டும்; நான் என் மனைவியோடு சேர்ந்து இந்த மாலைப் பொழுதில் விருந்து கொண்டாடுவேன்.
ai.explanation: The speaker, a soldier away on a military campaign, expresses his eager desire to return home. He wishes for the king to quickly engage in battle, secure victory, and grant him permission to leave. Once released, he anticipates reuniting with his wife at home and joyfully celebrating a feast together in the evening. The repetition of 'கலந்து' (having joined) elegantly contrasts the harsh joining of battle with the joyful joining of husband and wife.

ai.literal: One day like seven days will pass, to those who yearn keeping in mind the coming day of him who went far away.
ai.translation: For those who yearn, counting the days until the return of their lover who has gone far away, a single day drags on like seven.
ai.modern: நெடுந்தொலைவு சென்ற காதலர் திரும்பி வரும் நாளைக் கணக்கிட்டு ஏங்கித் தவிப்பவர்களுக்கு, ஒரு நாள் ஏழு நாட்களைப் போல மிக நீளமாகச் செல்லும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet captures the psychological experience of time for a waiting lover. The phrase 'ஒரு நாள் எழு நாள் போல் செல்லும்' (one day passes like seven days) vividly illustrates how time seems to stretch and slow down during periods of intense longing. The lover is described as 'சேண் சென்றார்' (he who went far away), emphasizing the physical distance that fuels the emotional pain. By 'வரு நாள் வைத்து' (keeping the day of return in mind), the poem shows how constantly calculating the time of reunion only deepens the yearning.

ai.literal: If obtained what is the use, if obtained what is the use, if united what is the use, if the heart having broken is destroyed?
ai.translation: What is the use of his returning, what is the use of receiving him, and what is the use of uniting with him, if my heart has already broken and perished?
ai.modern: என் உள்ளம் உடைந்து அழிந்த பிறகு, அவர் திரும்பி வந்தால்தான் என்ன, அவரைப் பெற்றால்தான் என்ன, அவருடன் கூடினால்தான் என்ன பயன்?
ai.explanation: The speaker expresses the urgency of her lover's return. She asks what good it would do if he returns, if she receives him, or if they unite, once her heart has already broken and perished from sorrow. The repetition of 'what is the use' emphasizes her desperate state and the futility of a delayed reunion. The words 'having broken' and 'destroyed' vividly portray the fragility of her enduring heart.
